facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass with anaplastic cells and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports this diagnosis.
The absence of pigmentation in the tumor and the positive reactivity to melanocytic markers are consistent with this subtype of melanoma.
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells, indicating high proliferative activity characteristic of anaplastic melanoma.

rationales.F02: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma, particularly of the caruncle.
rationales.F05: The histopathological finding of a solid tumor with an inflamed crust and large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity is highly indicative of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F06: The positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A is a strong indicator of a melanoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells is highly suggestive of an anaplastic melanoma.
rationales.F12: The immunoreactivity of melanoma cells to Melan-A is a strong indicator of a melanoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and a high proliferative index, supports the diagnosis of malignant melanoma of the caruncle, with amelanotic melanoma being a close runner-up due to the amelanotic nature of the tumor.
